run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-17T07:37:41Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning on otel-demo/frontend is explained by the cart datastore. A Chaos Mesh Schedule, otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress in namespace chaos-mesh, began spawning StressChaos experiments at 07:36:35 that applied memory stress to the valkey-cart container in pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft; the container's memory limit is only 10Mi. The container was OOMKilled (last termination: exitCode 137, reason OOMKilled at 07:40:40), restarted 4 times and is now in CrashLoopBackOff with the pod not Ready, so the valkey-cart Service has no ready endpoints. The cart service then logged 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' from 07:37:46 onward, and its gRPC handlers (POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, GetCart, EmptyCart) returned error spans; checkout's calls to CartService/GetCart and CheckoutService/PlaceOrder also errored, and frontend's /api/cart, /api/checkout and CartService client spans errored starting in the 07:37:41 bucket. frontend error span share was 4.61% over the 900s ending 07:56:27, versus zero error spans in the buckets before 07:32:41. ad, accounting and payment showed zero error spans in the same window; recommendation and fraud-detection kept their pre-existing ~1-per-10-minutes low-level errors that were already present before 07:37:41.

claims.text: frontend spans carry status codes STATUS_CODE_ERROR and STATUS_CODE_UNSET; the 900s-increase of error spans by span_name was 0 at the 07:32:41 evaluation and non-zero from the 07:37:41 evaluation, concentrated on GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout and the client spans grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (the 07:37:41 bucket already shows 1.03 AddItem/GetCart, 1.03 POST, 2.07 executing api route /api/cart).

At 07:56:27 the error-span share of frontend was 4.61% (100 * error increase / total increase over 900s), and the frontend 600s error increase rose from 0 in the buckets up to 07:32:41 to 8.42 at 07:37:41, 429.47 at 07:42:41, 816.91 at 07:47:41 and 377.47 in the last bucket.

Error-span increase over the 900s ending 07:56:27 by service was: frontend 444.83, frontend-proxy 431.30, cart 133.67, checkout 48.06, recommendation 1.12, fraud-detection 1.11, and 0 for ad, accounting and payment.

The failing operations are cart's own server spans (POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 124.75 error spans, POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 103.94, POST /oteldemo.CartService/EmptyCart 1.13 over 1800s) and checkout's client spans to the same dependency (oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 17.6, oteldemo.CartService/EmptyCart 1.13) plus checkout's own oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 31.9 and HTTP POST 14.3.

cart pod cart-755465879b-4p8d9 logged 'Successfully connected to Redis' at 07:36:58.1337024Z, then 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' at 07:37:46.3372017Z, alternating with 'Connection to redis was restored successfully.' / 'Successfully connected to Redis' through 07:39:09 and failing again from 07:39:42 to 07:39:58; the same 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' plus 'Error status code ...' lines continue at 07:44:30-07:45:04.

Pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft container valkey-cart has restartCount 4, ready=false, state waiting reason CrashLoopBackOff, and lastState terminated with exitCode 137, reason OOMKilled, finishedAt 2026-11-17T07:40:40Z; the pod's Ready and ContainersReady conditions are False (reason ContainersNotReady) since 07:40:40Z.

Deployment valkey-cart (image valkey/valkey:8.1.3-alpine, 1 replica) and its ReplicaSet valkey-cart-58df56c79c both specify container resources limits cpu 10m / memory 10Mi and requests cpu 2m / memory 4Mi.
Service valkey-cart in otel-demo has no ready endpoints: its only subset contains notReadyAddresses 100.96.5.138 (targetRef pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft, port 6379) and an empty addresses list.

Chaos Mesh Schedule otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress in namespace chaos-mesh spawned experiments at 07:36:35 (otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress-flgz4), 07:37:35 (ckxt6), 07:38:35 (w8p5x), 07:39:35 (nt6th), 07:40:35 (95xf6), 07:41:35 (ltcpd), 07:43:25 (v75mv) and 07:44:20 (psc57), with 'Forbid spawning new job because ... is still running' warnings between spawns.

The spawned StressChaos objects report 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft/valkey-cart' at 07:36:35, 07:37:35, 07:38:35, 07:39:35, 07:40:35 and 07:43:25, each followed by TimeUp/Recovered roughly 55 seconds later; later experiments ltcpd (07:41:35) and psc57 (07:44:20) failed with 'Failed to apply chaos: ... no running task found: task 26cfff7d... / bf44a508... not found'.
The kubelet emitted a BackOff warning for pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft ('Back-off restarting failed container valkey-cart ...') first at 07:37:39, repeated 22 times through 07:44:57.

frontend-proxy's own error spans are limited to 'ingress' (415.78) and 'router frontend egress' (15.52) over the 900s ending 07:56:27, i.e. the proxy records errors on the same frontend traffic rather than an independent failure mode.

All other otel-demo pods are Running and Ready with 0 restarts, including cart-755465879b-4p8d9, frontend-675fd7b5c5-x9gbm, checkout-5dccddf8bb-2ktmw and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-4ctlp; valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft is the only pod listed with ready=false and 4 restarts.
ad, accounting and payment each had 0 error-span increase over the 900s ending 07:56:27, so nothing in the observed data ties them to this incident.

recommendation (1.05 per 600s) and fraud-detection (1.05 per 600s) already had low-level error spans in the 07:17:41/07:22:41 buckets, before the 07:37:41 deviation, and their rate stayed essentially unchanged afterwards, so these are background errors rather than impact of this fault.

Hypothesis that frontend itself is the origin of the failures is rejected: frontend's pods are Ready with 0 restarts, its error spans are its /api/cart, /api/checkout and downstream CartService client spans, and the cart->redis connectivity failure is independently logged by the cart container from 07:37:46 while valkey-cart was OOMKilled.
Hypothesis that the cart service pod itself crashed or restarted is rejected: cart-755465879b-4p8d9 is Running and Ready with restartCount 0; its errors are raised when it fails to reach redis.

The 10Mi memory limit (and 10m CPU limit) on the valkey-cart container is why the injected memory stress produced an immediate OOMKill (exitCode 137) instead of just slowness; the limit is far below a valkey working set, but the stressor's own memory parameters could not be read to confirm the exact amount allocated.

The alert remains firing because valkey-cart has not recovered: after the OOMKill at 07:40:40 the container stayed in CrashLoopBackOff, its pod stayed not Ready, and the valkey-cart Service had only a notReadyAddress at 07:57, so cart continued to fail redis connections through 07:45 and frontend error spans were still elevated at 07:56:27.

Advisory: suspend or delete the Chaos Mesh Schedule otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress in namespace chaos-mesh so no further memory-stress experiments are spawned against valkey-cart, and confirm no further otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress-* objects are created.

Advisory: raise the valkey-cart container memory limit well above its real working set (currently limits.memory 10Mi, requests.memory 4Mi) so the datastore does not OOM under normal or stressed load, then verify the pod becomes Ready and the valkey-cart Service endpoints show a ready address.

Advisory: after remediation, verify recovery from the observed signals - cart logs stop emitting 'Wasn't able to connect to redis', cart's POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem and GetCart error spans return to zero, and frontend's STATUS_CODE_ERROR span increase returns to the pre-07:37:41 level of zero.

gaps: The Chaos Mesh Schedule object otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress itself could not be read: the chaos-mesh 'schedules' resource is not in the authorized Kubernetes kind list, so its spec (target selector, stressor memory size, workers, schedule interval, duration) is known only from its events.

Jaeger returned no traces for service frontend in 07:50:00-07:56:27Z (traces_search and traces_search_by_tags both empty), so span-level error messages/exception details for the failing frontend requests were not observed.

fetch_pod_logs returned no lines for the frontend container (frontend-675fd7b5c5-x9gbm) and for the valkey-cart container (valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft) in the requested windows; frontend's own log text and valkey's own log text are therefore unknown, and frontend impact rests on its error-span metrics.
Queries for networkpolicies and resourcequotas in otel-demo returned no objects; that absence cannot be asserted as fact, so a network-policy or quota contribution was neither confirmed nor excluded.

A FailedKillPod warning at 07:35:29 and a Killing event at 07:35:30 name pod cart-9fd895bb7-m7zfz, which does not exist in the current pod list; whether that event relates to this incident could not be established.
The change_history integration is not available, so who or what created the Schedule otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress and when it was created cannot be verified.

Metrics for currency, email, image-provider, kafka, load-generator, product-catalog, quote and shipping were not returned by the error-by-service query, so their state during the incident is unknown rather than healthy.
next_steps: Inspect the Chaos Mesh Schedule otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress spec (chaos-mesh namespace) with a tool that can read schedules, to confirm its target is valkey-cart and to record the stressor memory size and duration.
After the Schedule is suspended, confirm valkey-cart restarts stop, the pod becomes Ready, and the valkey-cart Service gains a ready endpoint address.
Right-size valkey-cart's memory limit/request and, if memory stress is still wanted for testing, scope it so it cannot exceed the container limit.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.

view.series_note: traces_span_metrics_calls_total counts spans of every operation of the service (internal, client and server spans alike), summed over the labels kept in this query; it is not a count of requests. status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET means the span carried no status; it does not mean the call succeeded.
